input.text: Welcome to Beihai Park — one of the oldest imperial gardens in China, over a thousand years in the making. Right in front of you, across the water, rises its icon: the White Dagoba, a Tibetan-style stupa built in 1651 by the first Qing emperor to honor a visit by the Dalai Lama. The lake itself — Beihai means "Northern Sea" — was the playground of emperors for centuries: they boated in summer and skated across the ice in winter. This garden perfected a Chinese art: recreating an entire imaginary world in miniature — islands as immortal mountains, water as the sea. Look for the Nine-Dragon Wall near the north shore, one of the finest glazed-brick walls in China, its nine dragons each a different color. locals come here at dawn to dance, sing opera, and practice calligraphy with water brushes on the stone paths. Join the morning; it's magical.
